cards.front: What a confidence score is for
cards.back: A decision input: answer, hedge, escalate to a person, or retry with a bigger model. Useful only if calibrated and acted on.
Whether one chunk clearly wins. Fooled when two copies of the same table look like a tie.
They score how likely the wording is, so fluent wording of a wrong fact still scores high.
The model saying "I'm 90% sure". Known overconfidence makes it weak evidence on its own.
Start with a hand-weighted average; once you have a few hundred labelled outcomes, fit a logistic regression. Hard rules like a calculator mismatch run first.
Sample the same question N times (often 5) above temperature zero. Samples agree when the model knows; they scatter when it guesses.
Entropy over meaning clusters of the samples: 0 when all agree, log₂ 5 ≈ 2.32 when all 5 differ.
Of all answers scored 0.7, about 70% are correct. A cosine of 0.83 is not 83% likely to be right.
Expected calibration error: Σ (nᵢ / N) · |accuracyᵢ − confidenceᵢ| over score bins.
Temperature divides the logit by T; Platt fits σ(a·logit + b) and can shift scores down; isotonic is most flexible but needs about a thousand labels.
A cost decision: minimise cost_wrong × wrong answered + cost_escalation × escalated, with per-segment thresholds and a hedge band.
After a new model or index, it usually means the score distribution moved, not that the system improved. Re-fit calibration.

quiz.q: What should happen when confidence is in the middle band?
choices: Hedge: answer with a caveat or ask a clarifying question
quiz.why: The middle band gets a hedge rather than a full answer or escalation.

quiz.q: Why is a rerank logit of 7.2 not a probability?
choices: It orders results but isn't calibrated to accuracy
quiz.why: Raw scores order results; calibration maps them to accuracy.

quiz.q: Your system is overconfident. Which calibration method can shift scores down?
quiz.why: Platt's bias term b can shift scores, while temperature only stretches around 50%.

quiz.q: Five samples give five different answers. What is the semantic entropy?
quiz.why: log₂ 5 ≈ 2.32 is the value when all samples differ.

quiz.q: The calculator result doesn't match the XBRL value, but the blended score is high. What happens?
choices: Answer, since the score is high
quiz.why: A calculator mismatch escalates whatever the blend says.

quiz.q: What decides where the answer/escalate threshold sits?
choices: Cost of a wrong answer vs the cost of a person's time
quiz.why: It is selective prediction: trade coverage for accuracy by cost.

choices: After any model or index change
quiz.why: Model or index changes move the score distribution.
